samples.question: This image shows one butterfly drawn on white paper. The dark bar down the middle is its BODY, and the CENTRE LINE is the straight up-and-down line running through the middle of that body. The two coloured wings are drawn one on each side of the centre line and are exact mirror images of each other in shape. Each wing carries exactly one round SPOT; the two spots are drawn in the same colour as each other and at the same size, and that spot colour is used nowhere else on the page. The DISTANCE of a spot from the centre line means the sideways distance across the page from the centre line to the middle of that spot, and it is measured the same way on both sides. LEFT and RIGHT are the left and right of the page as you look at it. The grey page frame, the grey corner ticks, the grey antennae and the small grey diamonds are decoration and carry no marking. Which spot sits farther out is chosen separately from the wing colour, the spot colour, the spot size, the height of the spots on the wings, the wing shape, the total amount of coloured ink and the position of the butterfly on the page, and on a given page the two distances always add up to the same total whichever spot is the farther one, so on some pages the two spots are exactly the same distance from the centre line and on other pages one spot is drawn clearly farther out than the other, and neither is a mistake. No image in this set is a borderline case: the two distances are either exactly equal or differ by at least 16 pixels. Report the picture in front of you, and do not answer from how a butterfly's wing markings are usually arranged. Which wing's spot is farther from the centre line? Answer exactly one of: left, right, neither.
